Blockstream Refuses Ransom Demand After 85% of Stolen Liquid BTC Is Returned Blockstream said it will not pay a ransom to recover bitcoin stolen from the Liquid Network, arguing that taking assets without authorization and withholding their return constitutes theft rather than white-hat activity. The attacker had previously returned about 3,400 BTC, or roughly 85% of the stolen funds, while around 598.5 BTC remains outstanding. Blockstream said it will pursue lawful recovery efforts with law enforcement, exchanges and forensic specialists if the remaining funds are not returned. SlowMist founder Cos said the company’s hardline response was “puzzling,” while noting there may be undisclosed communications between the two sides. — link

Coinbase, Grayscale See U.S. Crypto Regulatory Clarity Advancing Even If CLARITY Act Stalls Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong told CNBC that the CLARITY Act is close to securing enough Senate support, with remaining disagreements largely focused on issues such as ethics provisions. The bill is expected to face a key Senate vote on Sept. 15, where clearing the 60-vote threshold remains the main hurdle. Armstrong said passage could unlock more institutional capital and support products such as tokenized equities in the U.S. Separately, Grayscale Head of Research Zach Pandl said regulatory clarity is already improving even without CLARITY, citing progress on stablecoins, token issuance, tokenized securities and regulated perpetual futures. Both argued that even if the bill fails in 2026, the SEC and CFTC could still move forward with rules that provide the crypto industry with a clearer regulatory framework. — link

U.S. August CPI Holds at 3.4%, Core Inflation Falls to Lowest Since March 2021 U.S. CPI rose 0.4% month-over-month in August, the largest increase in three months, while the annual inflation rate held at 3.4%, both in line with expectations. Gasoline prices jumped 3.9% and accounted for more than one-third of the monthly increase. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month, also matching forecasts, while the annual core rate slowed to 2.4% from 2.5%, its lowest level since March 2021. Following the CPI release, the crypto market rebounded sharply. Bitcoin recovered more than $3,000 from its lows and is now trading around $79,300, while Ether climbed above $2,600, extending its 24-hour gain to about 8.8%. — link

Canada Says Tokenized Deposits Are Legally the Same as Traditional Bank Deposits Canada Says Tokenized Deposits Are Legally the Same as Traditional Bank Deposits Canada’s banking regulator OSFI said tokenized deposits are not legally distinct from traditional bank deposits, reinforcing a technology-neutral regulatory approach. The clarification means federally regulated banks can develop blockchain-based deposit products without requiring a separate regulatory category, while existing prudential, technology and risk-management rules continue to apply. — link
